title: Nilpotent-free spaces of 3 by 3 matrices over the field with three elements
journal_fit: The exact extremal dimension of a finite-field matrix space, its explicit construction and structural analysis fit finite-dimensional matrix theory and its arithmetic and combinatorial aspects.
contribution: The paper proves that the largest nilpotent-free subspace dimension in 3 by 3 matrices over the field with three elements is five. A direct algebraic construction gives the lower bound, while a finite reduction and independently checked search establish the upper bound and refute the proposed six-dimensional construction in this case.

abstract_tex: We prove that the largest dimension of a linear subspace of the $3\times3$ matrices over the field with three elements whose only nilpotent element is zero is five. Thus the proposed existence, over every finite field, of a nilpotent-free space of dimension $n^2-\binom n2$ fails at $n=3$. An explicit five-dimensional example has a direct algebraic proof. For the upper bound, a complement to the strictly upper triangular matrices is the graph of a $3\times6$ coefficient matrix. A search tree covers all $3^{18}$ such matrices using $3{,}109{,}888$ nodes. We give the coverage proof and a complete independent C verifier. The accompanying Lean development formalizes the reduction and search soundness, with two compiled evaluations explicitly included in its trust base. We also describe the nilpotent cone in characteristic three as a quadric in a seven-dimensional quotient and give examples over the fields with two and five elements.
